title: W4 fold pin is vacuous: the interleaved-router test places the router BEFORE the seed, so the r2 skew mode is never reproduced and the kind filter is unexercised
detail: r2 W4's skew required the router to consume an id NEWER than the seed (apply_place after the spawn). Here the seed is the newest node (monotonic ids, topology.odin:137), so the newest-first walk takes it immediately — deleting the Terminal filter, or reverting to the old count-based walk-back, keeps this test green.
recommended_fix: Swap the fixture order: spawn the seed first, then place_router, so the junction holds the newest id and the walk must skip it; the old count-based walk-back then points at the router and the test fails. (Also fix the wrong id comments: actual ids are 3/4, not 6/7.)

title: W10 fold leaves start_run's pan-latch reset untested — r2 W10 explicitly asked to assert it
evidence:
app/main.odin:746 (inside start_run):
	app.input.panning = false // v2-camera-zoom: a fresh run closes any stray pan latch

grep for 'start_run' across app/*_test.odin, app/input/*_test.odin, app/render/*_test.odin: no matches — no test drives start_run.
detail: r2 W10's fix: "assert begin_draw/start_run clear an armed latch". r3 pins the predicate, release, begin_draw, modal, and suppress transitions, but deleting the start_run reset keeps every gate green.
recommended_fix: Add an app-layer pin: arm the pan latch on a fixture Input, call start_run, assert input.panning == false.
